title: A $111 million move into reserve, and a reserve cap
question: Where did the school district’s 2025-26 unrestricted deficit go, and how do its reserves compare with the cap its own budget describes?
finding: Of the $133.4 million fall in the district’s unrestricted general fund in 2025-26, $111.5 million was a transfer into the special reserve fund (Fund 17), which carries that sum as a reserve for economic uncertainties in 2026-27 and $0 in the two projection years. Counted the way the budget narrative describes the cap (unassigned general-fund balance plus Fund 17), reserves come to $163.1 million against 10% of spending, $136.2 million; the narrative says the district expects to meet the cap. It also projects an unrestricted shortfall of $26 million in 2028-29.
how: Form 01, the multiyear projection (Fund 17 lines and unrestricted net change), and the budget narrative of the June 2026 recommended budget; quotations are checked against the text.
limits: The narrative’s one-sentence description of the cap may leave out amounts the Education Code excludes, and the code is not on disk, so the comparison is a question for the district, not a finding of a breach. Moving money to a reserve fund is permitted and prudent; a deficit created by a transfer to reserve is not spending.
